It has reported no builder walk-aways, forfeitures or renegotiations since inception. Its constraint is capital: debt-to-capitalization 36% against a 33% target after $1.0B of 6.50%/6.75% notes and a new unsecured bank facility, and it will not issue equity below book ($35.24), so growth now comes from takedown recycling, a $250M buyback signals the stock is cheap, and the August 2026 amendments opened rentals. Lennar's founder rights (most-favoured rate, capital priority, pool caps of $50M/$25M at risk per pool) shape what Millrose can offer everyone else.
